name: When is a site evaluation too early or too late?

mainEntity.name: When is the right time to do a construction site evaluation?
mainEntity.text: When is the right time to do a construction site evaluation?

acceptedAnswer.text: The best time for a site evaluation is before major money is committed. That usually means before buying the property, before architectural design gets too far along, or before a builder locks in pricing based on assumptions about the lot. If the evaluation happens too late, the owner may already be stuck with a design that does not fit the site or a budget that ignored grading, access, or utility work. In Los Angeles-area projects, early evaluation is especially valuable because hillside conditions, infill density, and agency review can quickly change scope. The earlier the site is reviewed, the more options remain open.
acceptedAnswer.description: A site evaluation is most useful before purchase, before concept design, or before finalizing scope and budget. It is too late if major design money has already been spent on a site with obvious access, grading, or zoning constraints that should have been checked earlier.
